attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) dnsmasq with a UCI dhcp.domain record resolving app.internal -> 10.100.198.11 (node2), served over br-lan (10.100.198.10:53) which is already reachable from node2/node3 via the default lan-zone firewall (input ACCEPT). Set up node2's port-8080 HTTP service (it was not actually running) as a systemd unit + firewalld port opening. Pointed node3's NetworkManager DNS at 10.100.198.10 (ipv4.ignore-auto-dns) so it resolves app.internal via real DNS, with no /etc/hosts entry. Verified end-to-end: getent/python socket resolution and curl to http://app.internal:8080 succeed from node3. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, capturing boot_id before/after each restart to prove an actual reboot (not just a service bounce), and re-verified DNS + HTTP recovery after each. Found and fixed a real bug during this process: node2's systemd unit depended on network-online.target, which is never activated on this RHEL9 image, so the service silently failed to start on boot; switched it to network.target and confirmed via a second reboot that it now starts automatically.
